text:
Maria: heads-up — canary `canary-2062-rc3` is showing a p99 regression vs baseline starting ~10:12 UTC. baseline p99 ~120ms, current p99 ~162ms over the last 3m. can someone run a quick profile + confirm rollback criteria?
AJ: on it. I'll kick a 5m profiler and collect flame graphs. which threshold do we want to use for an automatic hold vs manual rollback?
Maria: earlier decision was: hold if p99 > +20% sustained for 5m, rollback if > +30% for 15m OR error rate spike. this is ~35% right now but just started. hold first, collect profiles.
AJ: running profiler: `scripts/profiler/run_canary_profile --id canary-2062-rc3 --dur 300 --out /tmp/canary-2062345800.perf.data`
CanaryBot: monitor update — p50 58ms p95 108ms p99 162ms error_rate 0.09% (window=3m) :warning:
Devon: tagging in — I'll look at kernel allocations and kv-cache miss rate. AJ, please also capture GPU utilization (nvidia-smi sampling) and the runtime debug logs.
AJ: uploaded artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-canary/profiles/2062345800/{perf.data,flame.svg,nsight.json}. GPU util avg 72%, no obvious throttling. kv-cache miss rate +6% vs baseline.
Leo: quick rule from ops: if hold triggers, freeze canary traffic for new model rollouts and escalate to infra. Maria — do we want to hold now?
Maria: yes — hold. please stop ramping and keep 10% traffic. AJ/Devon, run bisect against last 3 deploys if you suspect runtime/kernel change.
AJ: bisect started across commits [a1b2..d4e5], running perf node on one node now. first 10m sample attached.
Devon: preliminary: increased kv-cache evictions correlate with slightly higher batch sizes from the new batching heuristic in v2062. also saw small bump in mallocs at the runtime layer.
Maria: this points to config change; can we revert batching heuristic quickly? if not, rollback to v2061. what's ETA?
AJ: revert PR is tiny — can push and rolling restart will take ~8m to cut new pods and warm caches. rollback to v2061 via deploy pipeline is ~6m.
CanaryBot: automated check: hold condition met (p99 > +20% for 6m). marking canary as HOLD and notifying #eng-oncall.
Leo: given kv-cache miss and sustained p99, my recommendation is rollback now. we want traffic stability over the heuristic.
Devon: agree. heuristic rollout caused regressions in internal micro-batching. rollback to v2061 and then we can re-run profiling with smaller batch sizes.
Maria: ok final: rollback to v2061. AJ start rollback and post links. I'll notify product and SRE.
DeployBot: rollback pipeline kicked: job 4621. cutting canary traffic to 0 and deploying v2061. ETA ~7m.
AJ: rollback completed, job 4621 succeeded. canary traffic set back to 0, new canary instance running v2061. artifacts: s3://redwood-canary/rollbacks/2062345800/logs.txt
CanaryBot: post-rollback metrics: p50 56ms p95 105ms p99 118ms error_rate 0.02% (window=3m) — back to baseline. :white_check_mark:
Leo: verified across three hosts — p99 stable and kv-cache miss rate returned to baseline.
Maria: thanks all. Devon/AJ, follow up with smaller-scale A/B test for the batching heuristic and add a perf gate before ramping next time. I'll close the canary and create a follow-up ticket. :thumbsup:
Devon: will open ticket with repro steps and flame graphs.
AJ: will add a canary probe to capture kv-cache evictions in the next rollout.
Maria: closing thread, good catch everyone.
